paper.title: Properties of earthquakes generated by fault dynamics

headline: Burridge-Knopoff / Carlson-Langer 1989 (mechanical spring-block chain): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; primary ell=3.0 MLE moment exponent=1.72, spans 3.8 decades (max/median=6103); mean moment decreases with stiffness (1.63 > 1.25 > 0.60 over ell=[2.0, 3.0, 4.0])

verdicts.gate: P1 GR power law at ell=3.0: MLE moment exponent in [1.5, 2.5]
P2 heavy-tailed moments at ell=3.0: span >= 2.0 decades AND max >= 100.0x median
P3 stiffness controls scaling: mean event moment strictly decreases as stiffness ell increases

extra.numerics: velocity-Verlet (symplectic, energy-stable) with a fixed micro-timestep validated against the stiffest linear mode; stuck intervals jump analytically to the next threshold crossing; a runaway/non-finite burst would surface as a diagnostic, not be scored as an event
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the Carlson-Langer stick-slip earthquake statistics (Gutenberg-Richter small-event power law, heavy-tailed moments, stiffness-controlled scaling) and would catch an artifact

citations: Carlson, J. M. & Langer, J. S. (1989). Properties of earthquakes generated by fault dynamics. Physical Review Letters 62(22):2632-2635. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.62.2632.
Burridge, R. & Knopoff, L. (1967). Model and theoretical seismicity. Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America 57(3):341-371.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the Carlson-Langer stick-slip earthquake statistics (GR small-event exponent, heavy-tailed moment distribution, stiffness-controlled mean moment)
